pairs.reason: These are mirror-image sibling types — same two functions in opposite dominant/auxiliary order (Ni-dom/Fe-aux vs. Fe-dom/Ni-aux), yielding genuinely different childhood presentations and developmental arcs, and each page already cross-links the other as its explicit contrast case while both point to the existing parent `[[concepts/cognitive-function-development-arc]]`, so no new hub is needed.

Both pages define the identical concept (information asymmetry as the condition undermining welfare-theorem efficiency), cite the same Stiglitz/Akerlof/Spence lineage, and enumerate the same mechanisms (adverse selection, moral hazard) — the titles are synonyms, and Page B is simply the more developed version into which Page A's inequality and Hayekian-limitation sections should be folded.

Both pages define the same Clark–Chalmers thesis as their subject and differ only in which downstream applications they elaborate (design criteria + PIM/transactive memory vs. DSRP + cognitive load), so one should retire into the other with the distinct sections folded in as subsections.

Page A's entire thesis — the three-step light/mid/dark gradient, the chair-must-bridge rule, the same Van Duysen attribution, and the same light-oak-on-oak-floor failure case — is already stated in Page B's "Value Bridging (Chairs)" section, so A is a duplicate elaboration rather than a distinct concept; retire A into B (relocating the Wegner chair-back-visibility material to a chair-selection page or a subsection of B).

Page B explicitly names "too-many-platforms problem" as its own alias, and both pages share the same definition (competing platforms → overlapping mental topography), the same cause (VC-driven ecosystem lock-in), and the same MIKAI response (orchestration substrate + noonchi/sumimasen) — Page B is simply the fuller treatment, so Page A should retire into it.

They are distinct, well-defined metrics with different denominators (total standard deviation vs. downside deviation) — the Sharpe page serves as the baseline definition and the Sortino page as the author's preferred variant, so merging would collapse a meaningful derivation relationship, and both already live naturally under the existing risk-adjusted-return linkage without needing a new parent.

Page A defines the single-cycle mechanism (one investor→company→return loop) while Page B defines a distinct multi-layer network phenomenon built on top of it, and each page already cross-references the other in a coherent parent/child relationship with no redundant overlap beyond the shared 4–5 year GPU/exit facts.

These are two competing, mutually-contrasting affordability metrics — a ratio-based benchmark and a residual-based one — and each page's substance is largely its critique of the other, so merging would collapse a genuine conceptual opposition that the cross-links already express correctly.

Page A is the general analytical frame (surplus allocation as a variable, spanning all historical phases and both productive and extractive routings) while Page B is one specific value of that variable (the Phase-3 financialised routing, with its own causal mechanisms, diagnostics, and policy levers) — B is properly a child of A rather than a duplicate, so A should be promoted to the parent hub with B (and a productive-reinvestment sibling) beneath it.

Both pages describe the identical artifact — MIKAI's typed, user-owned graph of goals/cognitive state populated by passive behavioral signal and claimed as the data moat — differing only in vocabulary and which source they were synthesized from, so `intent-graph` should retire into the more specific `personal-intent-graph` (keeping B's RAG distinction, compounding properties, and travels-across-surfaces material).

These are complementary sibling specializations distinguished by a real technical and regulatory boundary (the ~1000V licensing threshold), each with its own market structure, project types, and strategic logic — they already cross-reference each other as contrasting paths rather than restating one concept, and no parent page is needed since "electrical contracting" would add a layer without adding content.

Page A is a MIKAI-specific architectural decision (two layers with different latency/quality targets and its design consequences), while Page B is the general neuroscientific model that grounds and justifies it — a rationale that stands on its own and applies beyond this one decision, so the right relation is the existing cross-link, not a merge.

These are explicitly contrasting sibling design paths — opposing wood temperatures and harmony logics (chromatic vs. temperature matching) — held as a live either/or decision in the loft project, so merging them would destroy the distinction the pages exist to hold.

Each page describes a type-specific variant of the same underlying structure — an NT social wound framed identically (mental model, classroom/party/club settings, SP-type dynamics, inferior-function layer) and defined by explicit contrast with the other — so they are non-overlapping siblings that belong under a shared parent like "NT social alienation" rather than merging or standing alone.

Beautiful deleveraging is one possible outcome at the terminal phase of the long-term debt cycle — a parent/child relation with genuinely different scope (a 50–75 year accumulation arc vs. a prescriptive policy mix at its peak), and the shared four-lever section is overlapping mechanism, not a shared identity.

Page A is a conceptual contrast between two representation types (including the semantic side, which B doesn't cover), while Page B is the method family that produces only the structural half — they overlap on shared MIKAI motivation (the `boost` constant) but neither subsumes the other, and they already cross-link correctly as related-but-distinct.

Page B explicitly frames the two as parent/child — economic rents is the broad microeconomic category of above-competitive income, while rent-seeking is one specific political/institutional mechanism that generates it — so they are distinct pages in a hierarchy rather than duplicates, and the parent already exists (B), which rules out HUB.

Page A is a general taxonomy of material-pairing strategies (the framework, applicable to any marble), while Page B is a historical catalog of specific verde combinations that instantiates that framework — a parent/child relationship with genuinely different content axes (strategy types vs. period-by-period evidence), so the duplicated designer-translation table should be pruned from B rather than the pages collapsed.

Page A is the broad multi-actor asymmetry condition (of which the buyer-only cupping gap is its own instance), while Page B is one specific downstream sub-gap nested inside it — a parent/child relationship where B's roaster-outcome mechanism, tech layer, and platform thesis would be lost or would swamp A if merged.

They are a thesis/antithesis pair — static Ricardian endowment-given advantage versus deliberately constructed advantage — and each page's substance (mechanisms, case studies, critiques) is defined by contrast with the other, so merging would collapse a distinction both pages exist to draw.

Page B is a taxonomy of five pairing strategies while Page A is a single cross-cutting constraint that those strategies are evaluated against — the principle is referenced by, not equivalent to, the taxonomy, so they stand as parent/child rather than duplicates.

Both pages explicitly describe a nesting relationship in which the long-term debt cycle (a 50–75 year domestic debt-accumulation arc) sits inside the reserve currency cycle (a multi-century arc of currency dominance and power transition), making them parent/child layers of Dalio's framework rather than one concept described twice.

Page B is the general parent framework (dominant-then-auxiliary arc across many types, with Ni-first as one of several sections), while Page A is a specific instance of it (INFJ Ni–Fe in depth), and Page A already links to B as its broader framework — a parent/child relationship, not duplication.

Labor share of income is a measurable distributional statistic that serves as one mechanism and evidence stream for productivity-wage decoupling, which is a broader phenomenon about median wage stagnation (also driven by within-labor inequality and cost-of-living effects) — a parent/child relationship, not identity.

Page A defines an analytical variable (where surplus flows, plus its hydraulic model and measurement method) while Page B is a historical periodization that *uses* that variable as one of its diagnostic axes — a parent-concept/applied-framework pair with substantially non-overlapping content (Phase 2/3 market structure, transition signals, four future paths), so merging would bury the general category inside a specific periodization.

Page A contains no mechanism that Page B lacks — it restates the same Dalio long-term debt cycle arc in thinner form (and even defers to it in its own opening line), so it should retire into `long-term-debt-cycle`, carrying over the June 2023 CPI-mapping context and the unresolved "check the timeline" thread.

The overload loop is the broader cognitive pattern (Ni outpacing Te selection, ending in scope explosion and freeze), while consolidation-as-displacement is one specific mechanism *within* it — a parent/child relationship the pages already encode via explicit cross-links, not two names for one thing.

Page A is Ostrom's general institutional-design pattern, while Page B is the user's broader synthesis that incorporates polycentricity as only one of three pillars (alongside constitutional invariants and rule-shaped markets) — a parent/child relationship, not the same concept.

Cloud capital is the asset/mechanism component *within* technofeudalism — a parent/child relationship where Page B already links to Page A as one of its structural features, and each carries distinct content (A: properties of the asset and its rent-diagnostic test; B: the regime-shift thesis, its evidence, and its critics).

Page A describes the descriptive cycle mechanics (how debt-driven expansion turns into deflationary contraction), while Page B describes a prescriptive policy outcome at one specific point in that cycle — the deleveraging phase — making them parent-stage/child-remedy rather than the same concept, and B's Hayekian objection and ugly-deleveraging contrasts have no counterpart in A.

They are opposing forces in the same argument — CUDA Ecosystem is the incumbent lock-in mechanism while Hardware Abstraction Layer is the class of technology that could erode it, and each page already cites the other as a distinct counterparty rather than restating it.

Both pages describe the identical core mechanism — Ni generating faster than Te can select/execute against, with Te losing a committed external target — and differ only in which downstream discharge they emphasize (over-structuring/freeze in A vs. Se escape in B) and in intervention granularity; their prescriptions are near-identical (pre-commit one concrete external action, reduce rather than add structure), so A should retire into B as a "scope explosion / freeze" branch alongside B's existing Te-Se and Ni-Fi branches.

Page B is the six-stage parent sequence and Page A is one of its stages (Stage 4) elaborated with its own phenomenology, ENTJ contrast, and eruption mechanics — a parent/child pair, not two names for one concept.
